Techtronics faces significant business risks in launching its new smartphone. From a market perspective, the saturated nature of the industry means intense competition for market share, while the uncertainty surrounding consumer adoption of the unique feature creates a high risk of low sales volume. If the feature fails to resonate, the company may struggle to differentiate itself from established competitors. Operationally, the rapid innovation cycle in the mobile sector poses a risk of premature obsolescence, potentially leading to inventory write-downs and reduced return on investment if the product becomes outdated before it can recoup development costs.
